newsitem.title: UK: UK orders monpolies inquiry on Energy Group bid.
newsitem.headline: UK orders monpolies inquiry on Energy Group bid.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government on Friday ordered a monopolies inquiry into an agreed 3.7 billion pound ($6.1 billion) bid by American utility PacifiCorp for Energy Group Plc, Britain's biggest electricity distributor.
It is the first time that a U.S. takeover of a British electricity company has been sent to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) for further investigation.
Under former Conservative Prime Minister John Major, Britain stood by and watched seven of its 12 regional electricity companies taken over by American firms.

But in a move which sent Energy Group's shares plunging 33.5 pence to 617.5p, Trade and Industry Minister Margaret Beckett said she was concerned about the deal and brushed aside advice from both the industry regulator and the Office of Fair Trading.
She said she was worried about what one analyst referred to as "the tangled web of regulation" of the country's biggest electricity supplier and fourth biggest power generator.
"The supply, distribution and generation of electricity is of fundamental importance to the UK economy," she said in a statement.
"I consider that the merger does raise important regulatory issues that would benefit from a thorough investigation by the MMC."

Energy Group controls electricity giant Eastern Electricity, which was bought in 1995 by the once-mighty industrial conglomerate Hanson. After Hanson's demerger in February, it spun off its U.S.-Australian Peabody Coal and Eastern under the name Energy Group.

Beckett said she had not been convinced by arguments put forward by the OFT and electricity regulator Stephen Littlechild, who said that on balance the merger should be cleared subject to assurances from the two companies to address regulatory concerns.
Nigel Hawkins, utilities analyst at brokers Yamaichi, said he was not surprised at the referral.
"It was seen as an even-money type of situation," he said.

The bid has been dogged by concerns that the deal might be hampered by the Labour government, which has been a fierce critic of the previous government's policy in a wave of takeovers in the electricity sector.
Eleven of the original 12 Recs set up at privatisation in 1990 have been snapped up.
Although Beckett said her general policy continued to be that mergers would be referred on competition grounds, she said regulatory issues would remain of key importance.

"I shall continue to examine mergers on a case by case basis and where, as here, I believe that as part of a wider public interest scrutiny, important regulatory issues are raised, I may decide that a reference is warranted," she said.
The MMC are to report on their investigation by November 21. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
